title: Introduce prompt stewardship and degradation heuristics CI gate
author: Priya Malik
release_notes: Adds a new CI gate that detects prompt-level degradation trends and suggests quarantine/rollback actions. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: We frequently see regressions that are concentrated on small prompt sets or particular intents. Existing CI gates trigger on snapshot-level metric regressions but lack the ability to attribute early-stage degradation to stewarded prompt groups or to suggest targeted mitigation. This PR adds a lightweight 'prompt stewardship' CI gate that tracks temporal degradation signals per prompt cohort and surfaces automated remediation suggestions.

What this PR does: implements a CI hook and evaluation adaptor that computes a temporal degradation score (TDS) per prompt cohort, produces a severity-weighted alert, and integrates with the existing CI gating layer to fail builds when the aggregated risk exceeds team-configured thresholds. The gate includes: (1) prompt stewardship metadata (steward_id, intent_tag, owner_contact) ingestion, (2) a sliding-window AUC-of-degradation metric (default 7 days) and short/long term slope comparison, (3) a quarantine suggestion engine that maps signal patterns to recommended actions (quarantine, pin-model, add-smoke-eval, lower-temp fallback), and (4) telemetry to the console for per-prompt traces and remediation history.

Design notes: the TDS combines three components: delta-normalized metric drop (relative to historical baseline), volatility multiplier (higher weight for low-variance cohorts), and exposure factor (traffic share estimate). Score = AUC_drop * (1 + volatility_norm) * exposure_score. We experimented with a few normalizers; chosen formulation balances sensitivity to small, high-impact cohorts. The gate is configurable via eval-config.yaml under gates.prompt_stewardship: threshold, window_days, min_examples, steward_whitelist.

Why unique: unlike past approaches that only look at cohort-level average changes, this gate reasons about prompt ownership and operational workflows: suggestions are actionable (contact steward, schedule canary, auto-quarantine) and the gate emits structured remediation suggestions to downstream tools (Slack/Linear webhook adapter). The gate is intentionally conservative by default (min_examples=50, threshold tuned to ~3% short-term AUC drop for high-exposure cohorts) to reduce false positives.

Files & tests touched: Adds unit tests for scoring logic and synthetic cohort simulations; adds a lightweight integration test that runs the gate against archived eval-replay data; adds docs with rollout steps and config examples.

How to review: focus on the scoring function (eval_harness/gates/prompt_stewardship/score.py), the CI hook adapter (eval_harness/hooks/prompt_stewardship_hook.py), and the webhook adapter for remediation (integrations/linear_and_slack/prompt_stewardship_notifier.py). The bulk of additions are test fixtures and documentation.

Checklist:
- [x] implement scoring and gate integration
- [x] unit tests for scoring edge cases (zero-variance cohorts, sparse cohorts)
- [x] integration smoke against eval replay pipeline
- [x] docs and config example
- [x] register Linear hooks for remediation suggestions

Rollout plan: feature flag gated on eval-config, opt-in for 2 weeks (monitor noise rate), then enable soft-fail (raise warnings but not block merges) for core models, then hard-fail for stewarded high-exposure cohorts after tuning window.

Notes & future work: planned follow-ups include an on-call routing integration (pager for critical stewards), richer remediation suggestions (automated rollback playbooks), and a UI in the console to triage stewarded prompts.

Related: Linear ENG-1427 (prompt-level regression tooling), PM-308 (product rollout plan).
